title: Russian missile and drone attack on Kyiv includes an Oreshnik missile and destroys the Chernobyl Museum
body:
Early on Sunday, 24 May 2026, Russia launched a massive missile and drone attack on Kyiv, causing fires and hours of explosions, according to NPR. Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko reported at least 2 people killed and at least 77 injured, with damage in every district of the city. Ukraine's air force said Russia used 600 drones and 90 missiles, and that Ukrainian air defenses intercepted most of the drones and more than half of the missiles.

Russia's Defense Ministry confirmed use of the Oreshnik, a hypersonic ballistic missile. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said it hit Bila Tserkva, about 50 miles south of Kyiv, the third time Russia had used the missile in the war. Culture Minister Tetyana Berezhna said the attacks damaged the largest number of Kyiv cultural institutions since the 2022 invasion. The Chernobyl disaster museum was destroyed, and one of the city's oldest markets burned.

Russia said the strike was retaliation for a Friday drone strike on a college in Starobilsk in occupied eastern Ukraine, which Russia's Emergency Situations Ministry said killed at least 21 people. Ukraine denied targeting the college. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the EU was sending more support to reinforce Ukraine's air defenses.
